**Why this before the fan.** The fan's cost and its informative density window are both set by one number I do not yet have: the **onset field**. Re-reading run 6 with `sdh_onset` over only its *adequately sampled* range (the 10 mT leg, B ≥ 1.0 T; below 1 T the 50 mT step Nyquists at just 7.2 T at 0.85 T and 3.6 T at 0.6 T, so the sub-1 T tone tracks there are aliased and inadmissible) returns `onset_b = 1.00 T`, **`censored@edge`** on the carrier tone (7.3 T, snr_max 96) — i.e. the record never captured the onset. That is exactly `landau-fan` step 1 lever (1): *"If the carrying tone is censored, the spot-check record never captured the onset — `onset_b` is that record's low edge, a valid lower bound for `B_lo`; a cheap low-field extension pins it before committing a long fan."* The lever is worth 10× in fan cost: at Δ(1/B) = 1/(3·F_L) and the n-axis ray-Nyquist floor at `B_lo`, an n = 1.2–3.2×10¹² fan prices at **1.9 h for B_lo = 1.0 T, 4.2 h at 0.7, 15.2 h at 0.3** — and the partner tone clears its 5-period bar only for n ≥ 2.8×10¹² at B_lo = 1.0 vs n ≥ 2.0 at B_lo = 0.6. Committing a fan on an eyeballed onset either buys a 15 h fan I did not need or a 2 h fan that resolves the ABAB partner at a single density (no F(n) trajectory ⇒ no call). 20 min settles it.

**What it also buys (triple duty).** (i) Concatenated with run 6 the record becomes 0.30 → 10 T at one density, **δF = 1/(1/0.3 − 1/10) = 0.31 T** — enough to separate the model's ABAB heavy tone (25.78 T), the 4th comb line of the 7.31 T partner (29.24 T) and F_L (33.09 T) from each other, all three of which are currently merged inside run 6's δF ≈ 1.1–6.7 T. The investigation allows a clean spot check to be decisive on its own. (ii) **Grid-change reproduction** (`sdh-spot-check` Verify, and Verify item 2 of the investigation's mandatory F_L-tone-origin discrimination): this leg is uniform in 1/B where run 6 was uniform in B, so any tone surviving both is not a sampling alias. That matters here — run 6's spectrum at B ≥ 1 T is a **harmonic comb of the 7.3 T tone out to 18×** (14.8 / 22.3 / 29.4 / 43.7 / 58.6 / 88.4 / 130 T, snr 21–116), the signature of a spike-train ρxx deep in the quantum limit (ν ≈ 3 for a 7.3 T pocket at 10 T), and comb members above the grid's Nyquist fold back into the band where the real pockets live. (iii) It leaves the magnet at 1.00 T, at or just above the fan's first row.

**Design.** Same spot as run 6 — n = +3.2×10¹² (the D = 0 line's electron end, 16 mV under the TG limit), D = 0, gates (V_tg, V_bg) = (+0.9836, +1.1663). B = 0.30 → 1.00 T **uniform in 1/B**, 233 pts, Δ(1/B) = 0.01006 T⁻¹ — run 6's own spacing at its 1.0 T edge, Nyquist 49.7 T against F_L = 33.1 T.
